Given the diagnosis hint 'weighted' and the risk of overfitting weights on only 3 windows, I will test a simple mean combination of the top models as a robust baseline before attempting more complex weighting schemes.
Test inverse error weighting on full pool to handle moderate ranking stability and high noise.

The series has very high trend and seasonality strength but low predictability due to noise. The current leader (a1) uses a simple mean on the top 5 models, which performed well. The previous weighted attempt on the full pool failed, likely due to weight instability in a noisy environment. To test if robustness can be improved by leveraging the strong consistency of the top performers without the noise of the tail, I will test a trimmed mean on the top 7 models. This reduces outlier impact compared to a simple mean while keeping more diversity than the top 5, potentially smoothing the forecast errors.

The current leader (mean on top 5) suggests that averaging robust performers is effective. Since the series has strong seasonality and moderate ranking stability, testing a broader pool with a robust combination method like DBA (Deep Bagging) or median might capture additional signal or reduce variance compared to the simple mean. I will test the median on the full pool to check if it outperforms the mean on the top-k subset, leveraging the "low predictability" and "moderate ranking stability" hints that favor robust aggregation over simple averaging of a small subset.
Test DBA aggregation on full pool to handle potential phase shifts and moderate ranking stability.

The series has very strong trend and seasonality components but low predictability due to noise. The current leader (mean on top 5) works well by averaging out noise while capturing the signal. I will test a robust weighted combination using the top-performing models from diverse correlation groups to mitigate correlated errors, specifically targeting the high-trend/seasonality regime with `inverse_error` weighting on the top 7 models which showed stability in the trimmed mean attempt.

The current leader (a1) uses a simple mean on a small, metric-ranked pool of top performers. To test if the ranking stability (moderate tau) and high noise suggest that a more robust aggregation or a different subset is needed, I will try a Median combination on the full pool. This tests the "outlier/robustness" hypothesis against the "best model dominance" hypothesis implied by the mean on top-k.

The series has strong seasonality and a clear trend, but moderate ranking stability. I created `pool8` (top 5 by SMAPE) which includes THETA, NaiveMovingAverage, ETS, ONLY_CWT_catboost, and ARIMA. Testing a simple mean on this specific top-5 pool is a logical next step to see if refining the pool composition improves upon the previous best (`mean` on `pool4`).

The series has very strong trend and seasonality components with moderate ranking stability (Kendall tau 0.368). The current leader (a1) uses a simple mean on the top 5 models, which worked well by averaging out individual model biases while retaining high-signal models. To test if weighted combination can further improve upon this baseline given the moderate stability, I will use `weights_inverse_error` on the same pool of top 5 models (`pool4`) to see if emphasizing the lower-error models (ETS, ARIMA) helps.

The series has very strong seasonality and a high-ranking stability among the top performers (ETS, ARIMA, THETA). The current leader is a simple mean on a tight pool of 5 models. To test robustness against potential model-specific biases in this tight pool, I will evaluate a trimmed mean on the same pool to reduce the impact of any single outlier forecast.

The series has strong seasonality and a high-ranking stability among top models. While simple mean on pool4 is the current leader, using softmax weights on this same tight pool (pool4) tests if we can slightly improve upon uniform averaging by giving more weight to the stronger models (ETS/ARIMA) based on their validation performance, addressing the moderate ranking stability and low predictability.

The series has very high trend and seasonality strength (near 1.0) but moderate ranking stability, indicating that while ETS/ARIMA are strong, their relative performance fluctuates. The current leader (a1, mean on pool4) performs well. To test a different strategy that might handle the "mixed" regime better by adapting to recent model degradation/improvement trends rather than just static error or uniform averaging, I will use `weights_error_trend`. This weight method specifically targets cases where models improve or degrade over time, which fits the moderate stability profile.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8988. Series context: trend strength 0.9983 and seasonal strength 0.9999; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.368); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.332.
